Authors: K Yévenes, E Pianca, E Bonollo
Title: Designing for Arthritis and Activities of Daily Living: A Taxonomic Review of Hand Grasp Techniques in a Domestic Context
Abstract: The essential daily actions performed by humans in undertaking everyday chores are often referred to as activities of daily living (ADLs). ADLs frequently involve interactions with equipment, tools, products, and appliances to facilitate independence in one's senior years. Industrial Designers generate this equipment and, hence, it is desirable for designers to understand the range of hand grasp postures employed by older persons, particularly when afflicted with declining dexterity.
